preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or have gained owner privileges) to enable trading and set LP burn parameters
Attacker must hold some MARVIN tokens to interact with the liquidity pool
Trading must be active (owner must have called enableTrading())

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, enable trading and set LP burn parameters to maximize token burning frequency and percentage. Then execute trades through the Uniswap pair to trigger the autoBurnLiquidityPairTokens() function, which burns LP tokens and reduces total supply. The attacker can profit by holding tokens while the supply decreases (deflationary pressure) or by front-running the burn mechanism. Key steps: 1) Call enableTrading() as owner, 2) Use setAutoLPBurnSettings() to set high burn frequency (minimum 600 seconds) and high burn percentage (up to 10%), 3) Execute sell transactions to trigger the automatic burn function, 4) Monitor for price appreciation due to reduced supply.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has an automatic LP burning mechanism that can be controlled by the owner. By setting aggressive burn parameters (high frequency and high percentage) and then executing trades, the owner can trigger frequent burns of LP tokens, reducing total supply and potentially increasing the token value for holders. The attacker (as owner) can profit by holding tokens while the supply decreases.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the owner to gain control. 2. Enable trading. 3. Set maximum burn parameters (10% burn every 600 seconds). 4. Acquire MARVIN tokens. 5. Execute sell transactions to trigger the auto-burn function. 6. Profit from deflationary pressure.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank to impersonate the contract owner. 2. Call enableTrading() to activate the contract. 3. Call setAutoLPBurnSettings(600, 1000, true) for maximum burn. 4. Use deal() to give attacker MARVIN tokens. 5. Execute a sell transaction by transferring tokens to the Uniswap pair. 6. Advance time to trigger the burn. 7. Verify the attacker's balance increased due to deflationary effect.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: Since ownership is renounced, we cannot call owner-only functions like enableTrading() or setAutoLPBurnSettings(). However, if trading was already enabled before renouncement and auto-burn settings were already configured, we can still trigger the auto-burn mechanism by executing sell transactions.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Check current contract state (tradingActive, lpBurnEnabled, lpBurnFrequency, percentForLPBurn). 2. If trading is active and auto-burn is enabled, acquire tokens and execute sell transactions to trigger burns. 3. Profit from deflationary effect as supply decreases.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Read contract state to see if trading is active and auto-burn is enabled. 2. If not, we need to find another approach (maybe the vulnerability is that anyone can trigger burns under certain conditions). 3. Acquire MARVIN tokens (use deal() if possible). 4. Execute sell transactions to trigger auto-burn. 5. Verify that burns occur and attacker profits.
attempts.failure_reflection: The owner address is zero (0x000...000), which means ownership was renounced. We cannot impersonate the zero address to call owner-only functions. Need to check if trading is already enabled and if auto-burn is already configured.
